chapter_approach.intro: The chapter starts with a short story about Deba, Deep and their cows. Then you try their idea yourself at the gate. Each new idea has a short story or a picture. content.text:
A long long time ago, there was a cowherd family in Tarakeshwar.
Every day Deba and Deep took the cows out for grazing.
They used to return in the late evening together with all the cows.
One day, Deba asked, "How do we know that we have not lost any cows?"
They did not know how to count.
What could Deba and Deep do?

tool_config.title: Marks at the Gate
tool_config.learning_objective: Students mark each cow that leaves, strike out one mark for each that returns, and tell if any cow is missing.
tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. One big picture: the cow shed gate with Deba and Deep beside it, and a low plain wall for the marks. A small herd of the plan's own waits in the shed (the builder uses 6 cows, with a small Practice tag; no number is ever shown or said). FIRST, GET READY (picks up the opening story): the cows wait quietly in the shed behind the gate. A thought bubble with a question mark floats over Deba and Deep, the problem of the story. Their friend comes to the wall and says in a speech bubble: 'A mark for each cow that goes out. Strike one out for each that comes in.' Two small pictures show it: a cow walking out beside a new mark, and a cow walking in beside a mark with a thin line across it. The child taps Next. THEN, PLAY. Morning: one cow walks to the gate and waits. The child taps Make a mark: a mark appears on the wall and the cow walks out. This repeats for every cow. Evening: the line changes to 'Strike out one mark for each cow that comes in.' A cow waits at the gate. The child taps Strike out a mark: a thin line crosses one mark and the cow walks in. The last cow is slow and is still on the path when the others are in, so for a moment one mark has no line. The three What do you notice? prompts show one at a time in a speech bubble: after the morning, after the first cow is in, and while the slow cow walks. They are read and thought about; nothing is typed. LAST, THE BOOK QUESTION: when the last cow is in, 'Did all the cows come back home?' shows under the wall with two big tiles, Yes and No. Its three steps show beside the wall; step 3 is 'Look at the wall. Does any mark have no line across it?'. The child looks at the wall: no mark is without a line, and that answers step 3. That leads to the book question, and the child taps Yes. Every mark now has a line across it.

tool_config.title: Count the Big Herd
tool_config.learning_objective: Students count 47 marks in groups of five and find how many cows are still out and how many came home.
tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. The picture is the shed gate with a wall beside it and, in the last part, the stone slab on sand. Marks stand in groups of five with a gap and no slanting line across a group; a standing mark is a cow still out and a struck-out mark, with a thin line across it, is a cow that is back. A number pad (digits 0 to 9, a back key, OK) slides up only when a number is asked. FIRST, GET READY (the cowherds are back at the wall, one morning after the cows have gone out to the fields): Deba and Deep stand beside the wall. A short row of marks stands on it, labelled Practice, in two groups of five and one group of three, all standing. Deba asks in a speech bubble: 'Our wall again. How many marks are there?' The child taps each group: it lights up and shows its own count, 5, 5 and 3. The number pad slides up, the child types the marks on the wall and taps OK. THEN, PLAY (Practice): evening. 'Ten cows come home. Strike out their marks.' The child taps a group of five two times: five cows walk in each time and a line crosses each of their marks. Three standing marks are left. Line: 'Which marks are cows still out? Tap them.' The child taps the three standing marks and they glow. LAST, THE BOOK QUESTIONS, on the real stone slab. (1) ch1.fill1, 'So, they had ____ cows.': the slab holds nine groups of five and one last group of two marks. Each tap on a group lights it and shows only that group's own count; there is no running total. The child adds and types the number on the pad, then taps OK. (2) ch1.story4: the next day the cows walk in, five at a time. The child taps a group of five to strike it out, group after group. The last group of two stays standing. Deba and Deep look along the path and see no cow outside the gate. Then three answer cards ask 'Why were Deba and Deep worried?': 'Two marks were still left, but they saw no cows outside the gate.' (right), 'Every mark was struck out and every cow was home.' (wrong), 'There were too many marks to count.' (wrong). The child taps one card. A step of the plan follows: 'How many marks are still left? That many cows are still out.' The child types the number on the pad. (3) ch1.fill2, 'How many cows had reached home?': the child types the number on the pad. Last scene, after the answers: Deba and Deep find the missing cows in a nearby field and all walk home together; the last marks get their lines.

tool_config.title: Longest and Shortest Names
tool_config.learning_objective: Students count the letters in names to find the longest and the shortest name, and to see when two names are equally long.
tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. Tapping a name drops a small count mark under each letter in turn and a count badge grows. Names sit in rows of equal letter boxes, one letter in each box, so room does not mislead (in the first two parts, and in stage 1 and stage 3 of the book questions). In stage 2 the names are written freely, as the book draws them, so the child sees that a name can look wide and still have as many letters as a narrow one. A green tick badge and a green cross badge wait at the side, as many as needed. THE LETTER KEYBOARD AND ITS DONE KEY: the keyboard (A to Z, a back key and Done) slides up only when a name is asked. Whatever case the child types, the line shows the name with the first letter capital and the rest small. There is no space, digit or sign key, so only letters can be typed. The back key takes away the last letter. A friend's name holds up to 12 letters and an animal name up to 14; when the line is full the keys wait and a small line says 'The line is full.' Done stays grey until the line holds at least one letter. Tapping Done accepts the name: it is fixed on its line and its letters are counted at once. The tool counts whatever is typed and does not check that it is a real name or animal. A quick-pick name tile puts its name on the next free line at once and needs no Done. FIRST, GET READY (picks up the yard game of the story, where the child with the longest animal name goes first): two children of the yard each hold one Practice animal card, cat and horse, in equal letter boxes. The child taps each name to count its letters, then drags the green tick onto the child who goes first. Line: 'The longer name goes first. Count, then tick.' THEN, PLAY: three Practice names, hen, camel and buffalo, in letter boxes. The child taps each name to count it, then drags the green tick onto the longest name and the green cross onto the shortest name. Line: 'Tick the longest name. Cross the shortest name.' LAST, THE BOOK QUESTIONS, in three stages, in the book's order. STAGE 1, the team captains (ch1.letus1, ch1.longer1): the ten animal cards (tiger, dog, snake, goat, lion, elephant, deer, ox, rat, monkey). The child taps a card to count its letters; the count badge stays on the card. Two boxes wait, First team captain and Second team captain, each with a Letter count slot. The child drags one card into each box and its count travels with it; a card dragged with no count shows 'Tap the card to count its letters first.' Then 'Do you know any animal having a longer name than the first team's captain?': the keyboard slides up, the child types an animal name and taps Done, and the tool counts its letters and says if it has more letters than the first team's captain. Any word of 1 to 14 letters is accepted by Done; a word with 8 letters or fewer is counted and gets the message that it is not longer. tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. Two RINGS are this tool's own device: an orange ring and a blue ring, round outlines that the child drags onto one letter. A letter with the orange ring turns orange (the starting letter); a letter with the blue ring turns blue (the ending letter); all other letters stay dark grey. The letter keyboard and the quick-pick name tiles slide up only when a name is asked. CAPITAL AND SMALL LETTERS, ONE RULE: a letter counts the same whether it is capital or small. A typed name shows with its first letter capital and the rest small, whatever the child types, so Kartik, kartik and KARTIK are the same name. Starting-letter piles have capital labels and ending-letter piles have small labels, but a tag goes by the letter and never by the case: Kartik goes in pile K by its first letter and in pile k by its last letter. A tap on K in the alphabet strip means the letter K or k. THE CONFIRM STEP: the keyboard is the one of the last tool (A to Z, a back key, Done; only letters; 1 to 12 letters). The child types their name and taps Done. Done stays grey until the line holds a letter. Done confirms the name: it is fixed on a tag in grey letters and is the child's own name in ch1.letus3b, ch1.letus3c and ch1.letus3e. A quick-pick tile confirms its name at once. To change the name, the child taps the tag and types again; the rings and the counts for the own name then start again. There is no Check key: each drop of a ring or a tag and each tap on a pile or a letter is checked the moment it is made. A right drop stays. A wrong drop slides back with its message. Part ch1.letus3d is met when D and M both glow. FIRST, GET READY (a new place, so it does not repeat the name tags picture): a shelf of bird picture cards, each with its name under the picture. Practice cards: swan and owl. Line: 'Orange ring: starting letter. Blue ring: ending letter.' The child drags the orange ring onto the first letter of swan and the blue ring onto its last letter, then the same for owl. THEN, PLAY (Practice): a fruit stall with four Practice cards: mango, banana, guava and apple. Three piles wait, labelled with the ending letters a, e and o. The child drags each card onto the pile with its last letter. When the cards are sorted, the child taps the pile with the most cards. Line: 'Sort the cards by their last letter. Tap the tallest pile.' LAST, THE BOOK QUESTIONS. The eight Practice names are the book's friends: Deba, Deep, Hemant, Mahesh, Kartik, Teji, Jojo and Mala, each on a name tag with its first letter orange and its last letter blue. The child drags each of the eight tags onto the pile of its starting letter, then taps the pile that has the child's own starting letter to read its count. If the child's letter has no pile, the tool shows an empty pile with that letter and the count 0. (c) ch1.letus3d: the piles show their counts as stacks; the child taps the tallest pile or piles. D and M are the tallest and tie, so both must be tapped. (d) ch1.letus3e: the child drags the blue ring onto the last letter of their own name. (e) ch1.letus3f: an alphabet strip from A to Z. The child taps the six letters that start a name (D, H, J, K, M, T) to take them out. The 20 letters left glow and a line says they start no name. A last optional line: 'Try this later with the boys' names and the girls' names in your class.'

tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. Teji and Jojo stand beside the mat of the 27 number cards, the same as in the last tool. A laying row has two slots. The child lays the cards of a number and taps OK: the tool shows the written name with a grey hyphen, the numeral and the letter count, for example 5 + 3 = 8 letters. 'Which two cards have the same number of letters?' The child taps each card to count its letters, then drags the two cards with the same count into a box. THEN, PLAY (Practice): 'Find a number whose name has 4 letters.' The child lays the cards of a number and taps OK. Four, Five and Nine fit. Any other number shows its own letter count. LAST, THE BOOK QUESTIONS, six steps in the book's order. (1) ch1.example2: the book's words already say that 56 has 8 letters, and the screen does not hide that. The child's task is the counting: lay Fifty and Six (56), tap OK, and tap each card to see its letters counted; the tool shows 5 + 3 = 8 letters. (2) ch1.think1: 'Write other numbers between 1 and 99 that have 8 letters.' The child lays cards and taps OK. A number with 8 letters (not 56) joins a table of six boxes, each box showing the number and its name; any other number shows its own letter count. Every number with 8 letters is accepted. After three numbers are found the tool says that more numbers fit, and asks 'What is the same in the names of the numbers you found?' (read and thought about). (3) ch1.letus5: 'Write the number(s) between 1 and 99 that have the longest name.' The child lays cards and taps OK; 73, 77 and 78 (12 letters each) are accepted, and the tool says the other two fit as well. (4) ch1.letus6a: the first orange Find out box is shown on its own, without any other question above it. The child lays two cards and taps OK; 93, 97 and 98 are accepted. A number that fits the letters but is not near 100 gets a gentle message. (5) ch1.letus6b: the second Find out box, with a strip of the tiles 63 to 78. The child taps tiles to count their letters, then lays the answer and taps OK; 70 (Seventy, one card) is accepted. (6) ch1.letus7: a short OPTIONAL instruction card: 'Make similar puzzles of your own in your notebook and ask your classmates.' Nothing is entered; the child taps Next.

tool_config.screen: FRAME, the same in every tool: a Hint lamp and a Next arrow. No score, no timer. Teji and Jojo stand beside a table with picture cards and two group boxes (dotted boxes for picture cards, note-pad panels for the household objects). A rule card names the rule of a grouping; a card dropped in a group stays there until the child drags it out. FIRST, GET READY (picks up the cards story with other cards): four Practice cards, a red apple, a yellow banana, a red ball and a yellow ball. Teji's rule card says 'Fruits and toys' and two boxes are labelled Fruits and Toys. The child drags each card into its box. Line: 'Teji's rule: fruits and toys. Drag each card into its group.' THEN, PLAY (Practice, new cards): 'Find the rule.' Four Practice picture cards sit in two groups with no label: a hen and an owl in the first group, a cat and a horse in the second. Three rule cards wait: 'Birds and not birds', 'Fruits and toys' and 'Red things and yellow things'. The child drags one rule card onto the two groups. A right card labels both groups. LAST, THE BOOK QUESTIONS, three stages, in the book's order. STAGE 1, ch1.jojo1: Jojo's two groups of five cards are shown as the book draws them: a kite, an aeroplane, a bird, a fly and a drone in the first group, and a fish, a light bulb, a mobile phone, a book and a rat in the second group, with no label. Three rule cards wait: 'Things that fly and things that do not fly', 'Things that eat food and things that do not' and 'Things that live in water and things that do not'. The child drags one rule card onto the two groups. A right card labels both groups. STAGE 2, ch1.letus8: the eight household objects (TV, Chair, Lamp, Bed, Clock, Fan, Pillow, Blanket) and two lilac note-pad panels, 'Things that need electricity' and 'Things that don't need electricity'. The child drags each object into a panel. The split is fixed: TV, Lamp, Clock and Fan need electricity; Chair, Bed, Pillow and Blanket do not. STAGE 3, ch1.letus9: the same eight objects return to the table and two empty pale green panels with blue tabs wait, with no labels. The child drags every object into one of the two panels. Any grouping is accepted if every object is in exactly one panel, both panels hold at least one object, and the split is not the electricity split. Then the child drags a rule card onto the panels: 'Things that give light or show pictures' (Lamp and TV against the other six), 'Things that tell the time' (Clock against the other seven), 'Things that blow air' (Fan against the other seven) or 'Another rule: I say it aloud' (always fits). The tool checks the first three cards against the groups. When the groups and the rule card fit, a last line shows: 'Can you think of one more object for each group?'

tool_config.instruction: Put each card in a group. A rule decides the group.
feedback: Right try: Each card is in the group that fits the rule.
Wrong try: Look at this card again. Does it follow Teji's rule?
Right try: Yes. The hen and the owl are birds. The cat and the horse are not.
Wrong try: This rule does not fit every card. Look at each group again.
Right try (ch1.jojo1): Yes. The first group has things that fly. The second group has things that do not fly.
Wrong try (ch1.jojo1, eat food): A bird eats food, but a kite does not. They are in the same group, so this rule does not fit.
Wrong try (ch1.jojo1, live in water): Only the fish lives in water. The rule must fit every card in a group.
Right try (ch1.letus8): TV, Lamp, Clock and Fan need electricity. Chair, Bed, Pillow and Blanket do not.
Wrong try (ch1.letus8, the Lamp): This lamp has a pull cord. It is an electric lamp, so it needs electricity.
Wrong try (ch1.letus8, the Clock): A clock runs on electricity from a cell or from the plug.
Wrong try (ch1.letus8, the Fan or the TV): This object needs electricity to work. Try the other panel.
Wrong try (ch1.letus8): This object needs no electricity to work. Try the other panel.
Right try (ch1.letus9): Every object is in one group, and the groups are new. Your rule card fits.
Wrong try (ch1.letus9): This is the electricity split again. Group the eight objects another way.
Wrong try (ch1.letus9): One panel is empty. Put at least one object in each panel.
Wrong try (ch1.letus9): An object is still on the table. Every object goes in one group.
Wrong try (ch1.letus9): This rule card does not fit your groups. Pick another card, or move an object.

Tone, the same in every tool: a soft chime and 'Well done.' before a right reason; 'Not yet, try again.' before a wrong reason. A wrong try shakes gently and can be retried. No buzzer, no red cross, no score.
tool_config.done_when: First, the four practice cards are in the Fruits and Toys boxes. Then, the child has chosen the rule card that fits the two practice groups. Last, the child has chosen the rule card that fits Jojo's groups; has placed all eight household objects in the electricity panels; and has placed all eight in two new panels with a split that is not the electricity split, with a rule card that fits.

visual_key.tally_mark: one short upright bar with a thick stroke, one bar for each animal; on the stone slab the bars are black and stand in groups of five side by side with no slash (four groups to a row in the first two rows, then one group of five and one group of two); on the wall of the opening picture the bars are dark brown
visual_key.struck_mark: a tally bar with a thin black slanting line drawn across it; in the opening picture the struck-out bars are at the top of the block and the bars not yet struck out stand upright below them
visual_key.stone_slab: a rough reddish-brown stone slab with small grey specks and one thin crack, standing on yellow sand; it carries the marks for the many cows
visual_key.cow_shed: a low stone and mud shed with a red-brown tiled roof, a fence of rough wooden poles at the gate and a green bush beside it; the cows leave and re-enter through the gate
visual_key.cows: cows and bullocks in white, cream, orange, red, brown, grey and one magenta-pink, with short horns and pink noses; a white cow wears a small gold bell on a dark blue strap
visual_key.deba_and_deep: two cowherds with long dark curly hair, each with a tall wooden stick: one in a purple-brown robe with a dark belt and a cross strap, one in a plain ochre tunic with a brown sash and a cross strap (in the first picture this one wears a yellow cloth on the head); the book never says which is Deba and which is Deep
visual_key.their_friend: a young cowherd seen from behind in a light blue shirt with a bag strap and short dark curly hair, holding a stick; the book does not name him
visual_key.animal_card: a tilted white square card with a thick colour frame (tiger red, dog light green, snake yellow, goat cyan, lion light green, elephant light blue, deer magenta, ox lilac, rat pink, monkey magenta); the animal is drawn inside and its name is written in a handwriting font along the bottom edge
visual_key.name_big: a child's name written large in a thin handwriting font in dark grey on white, one name under the other: Mahesh, then Kartik; Mahesh is the wider word
visual_key.mahesh_kartik_boys: two boys, each pointing at one white speech bubble that says 'My name is longer.' (the bubble has a tail to each boy): one with black curly hair in a yellow shirt with red dots, one with short black hair in an aqua shirt with a green collar; the book does not say which boy has which name
visual_key.tick_and_cross: a round green badge with a white tick, and a round green badge with a white cross
visual_key.answer_blank: a dotted line or a pale yellow rounded box for the child's answer; on the number hunt, a pink bar for the number name and a green-outlined circle for the numeral; beside each friend's name line a small dotted circle
visual_key.number_card: a rounded tag-shaped card with the number word in a serif font: One to Nine on peach tags, Ten to Nineteen on light blue (cyan) tags, Twenty, Thirty, Forty, Fifty, Sixty, Seventy, Eighty, Ninety on light green tags (27 cards in all); a number name is made by laying the tens card first and the ones card after it, for example Forty, Three; every number from 1 to 19 is one card by itself (Seventeen); a hyphen is only in the written name (fifty-six), never on a card
visual_key.teji: a girl with black hair in two plaits tied with red bows, in a red dress with a blue collar and small pale dots
visual_key.jojo: a boy with black curly hair in a yellow T-shirt with a blue-green band across the middle
visual_key.place_sign: the BOOK's signboards: a yellow signboard with black letters in more than one script and in English capitals: VENKATANARASIMHARAJUVARIPETA (Telugu and Hindi above), IB (Odia and Hindi above) and OD (Gujarati and Hindi above); photographs in the book; the plan draws its own boards, see place_signboard
visual_key.girl_at_signboard: a girl with black hair and a blue hairband in a pink top who points at the long signboard; a pale blue thought bubble beside her says 1..2.. 3...
visual_key.picture_card: a tilted white square card with a thick colour frame and a plain picture with no name, used for sorting: a yellow bird, a black fly, a brown rat and a red, yellow and blue striped fish, and a blue drone, a white aeroplane, a blue mobile phone, a yellow light bulb, an orange book and a red and green kite; the frame colour of a card changes between the book's pictures, so the colour is not part of the card
visual_key.household_card: the same card style with the name in handwriting under the picture: TV (red frame; a remote on the floor), Chair (light green), Lamp (yellow; a pull cord at the base), Bed (cyan), Clock (light blue; a wall clock with a pink rim), Fan (magenta; a ceiling fan), Pillow (lilac), Blanket (pink)
visual_key.group_box: a rounded box with a dotted outline that holds the cards of one group; a writing group is a note-pad panel with spiral rings down its left edge and a coloured tab on top: lilac with the labels Things that need electricity and Things that don't need electricity, or pale green with blue tabs and no labels; four lines in each panel
visual_key.mala: a schoolgirl with dark brown hair in two ponytails, in a blue pinafore with a yellow satchel on her way to school; her face with two ponytails is also drawn close up, in a red top and a yellow vest
visual_key.mala_mother: a woman in a green sari with a red bindi, seated, combing the hair of a small girl who sits in front of her
visual_key.hair_style_pictures: six head-and-shoulder pictures in pale green table cells: one high ponytail; two long plaits with blue ribbons; short curly hair; wavy hair with a blue hair clip; short straight black hair swept to one side; two low ponytails
visual_key.hair_page_children: five small unnamed children beside the text: a curly-haired boy in green, a wavy-haired girl with a blue clip in pink, a boy with short black hair in blue, a girl with a high black ponytail tied with orange in yellow, a curly-haired boy in light blue
visual_key.speech_bubble: a white rounded bubble with a thin black outline and a pointed tail, serif text; the thought bubble is a pale blue cloud with 1..2.. 3...
visual_key.first_last_letter_colours: the first letter of a name is orange and the last letter is blue, every other letter dark grey, all letters the same size; the same two colours on the Name Tags picture, on the Starting and Ending Letters tool and on the review picture; green is kept for the tick badge, so no green ring; the colours are this plan's own convention, the book has no name tags and no such colours
visual_key.wall_marks: the wall of the first page: a low plain wall of stone and mud beside the cow shed gate with a block of dark brown upright bars on it (see tally_mark and struck_mark); the plan's own short rows on the Marks at the Gate tool and in the Marks on the Wall story use the same bars, never the 47 of the stone slab
visual_key.tally_group: five upright bars side by side with a clear gap before the next group, as the stone slab draws them; NO slanting line across the group, because in this chapter a slanting line means struck out; the last group may have fewer than five bars
visual_key.sheep: a real sheep: a thick woolly cream-white fleece, a dark brown face and legs, small ears, a short tail; smaller than a cow and drawn in the same style as the cows; never a cow, a goat or a cloud; the book names sheep but never draws one
visual_key.hemant: Hemant, drawn by the plan because the book names him once and never draws him: a young cowherd with short dark curly hair in a green shirt (a colour no other cowherd wears), holding a stick; not the friend in the light blue shirt; his cows and his sheep stand with him
visual_key.name_tag: a plain white rounded tag with a thin dark outline hung above a school bag hook, one child's name on it in the book's thin handwriting (name_big), first letter orange and last letter blue (first_last_letter_colours), all letters the same size; the same look on every picture of the chapter
visual_key.place_signboard: the plan's own signboards: three plain yellow boards on short posts by a road, drawn blank (the first board far longer than the other two, which are small and about the same size); the picture maker generates no text at all. OVERLAY TEXT FOR THE BUILDER ONLY, never put in a generation prompt: afterwards the English capitals VENKATANARASIMHARAJUVARIPETA (long board), IB (second board) and OD (third board) are added as typeset black text, spelled exactly, one font, the same letter height on all three boards, so each board is as long as its name; no other script is drawn
visual_key.class_children: twelve unnamed children of the plan's own practice class, drawn in the book's picture style, in two rows of six (the back row on a low bench, high enough that each back-row child shows from the chest up above the heads of the front row), in school clothes, each whole from the chest up in three-quarter view so the hair style shows; each child has exactly one of the six styles of hair_style_pictures, and children of one style are drawn with identical hair wording (children 2, 7 and 12 all have short straight black hair swept to one side); shirt colours vary and do not follow the style; no child is hidden; no number, ring or tally on the picture. CHECK DATA FOR THE BUILDER ONLY, never drawn and never put in a generation prompt: the true counts in the table order are high ponytail 3 (children 1, 8, 11), two long plaits 2 (3, 10), short curly 2 (4, 9), wavy with a clip 1 (6), short straight swept to one side 3 (2, 7, 12), two low ponytails 1 (5); 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 12; the answer of ch1.letus10 is labelled From the picture
visual_key.number_name_row: a number name laid out with number cards: the tens card on the left, the ones card on the right with a small gap, no hyphen between them; a number from 1 to 19 is one card alone; the cards look exactly like number_card
visual_key.letter_rings: two round rings that only the Starting and Ending Letters tool uses, as its own device: an orange ring and a blue ring, each big enough to go round one letter of a name; the child drags the orange ring onto the first letter and the blue ring onto the last letter, and the ringed letter shows in the ring's colour (orange for the starting letter, blue for the ending letter) as on the name tags; no green ring, because green is for the tick badge; the Name Tags picture draws no rings, only the coloured letters

story.thread: Deba and Deep, two cowherds of Tarakeshwar who do not know how to count, keep track of their cows with one mark on the wall for each cow that leaves and one strike-out for each cow that comes back; then Teji, Jojo and their friends count the letters in names and in number names, and sort things into groups by a rule.
story.setting: the village of Tarakeshwar: a cow shed with a tiled roof and a gate, a wall and a stone slab with marks, the grazing fields; then a classroom and home: name cards, number cards, picture cards, household objects, and the hair styles of children going to school
